No application code in this directory — only `.claude/skills/` and `CLAUDE.md`. I scored the premise as you stated it, not your actual S3 call sites.

**What I found.** Don't build it (the record calls this DROP). The deciding fact is your own sentence: S3 is the only store and no second one is named, so the interface would ship with exactly one implementation — the skill library classifies that as *generality without instantiation*, an abstraction absorbing a variation that doesn't exist. `functionality-complexity-tradeoff` §8a makes the test explicit: optionality counts only when the next implementation is **named and probable**; speculative optionality loses to YAGNI.

**Why it matters.** Building it costs a type, a factory/wiring seam, a second set of tests, and a permanent translation layer every future S3 feature must pass through — paid on every change, for a payoff with no date. The sharper cost: a single-implementation interface gets shaped by the only thing behind it, so it ends up carrying S3 semantics (presigned URLs, multipart, storage classes, lifecycle rules, consistency model). When a real second vendor arrives, the shape is wrong and you redesign anyway — so the insurance mostly doesn't pay out. Not building it costs you little: the swap work you'd defer is real but bounded, and it's cheaper once you know the second vendor's actual semantics. The risk of skipping is only that S3 calls scatter through business logic, which is a separate and cheaper problem to prevent.

**Do this first.**
1. Keep every S3 call inside one module (e.g. `storage/s3.ts` or `storage/s3.py`) with functions named for your domain operations — `put_upload`, `get_upload_url` — and no `boto3`/`@aws-sdk` import anywhere else. That's plain boundary hygiene, not a polymorphic abstraction: one file, no interface, no factory.
2. If the real motive is testability, fake at that module boundary or run MinIO/`moto` locally — don't add a production abstraction to serve tests.
3. If a second store is actually on someone's roadmap, say who and when; a named, dated second vendor flips this verdict to BUILD-minimal.

**What I did not check.** Whether S3 calls are already scattered — run `grep -rE "boto3|@aws-sdk|aws-sdk" --include="*.{ts,js,py}" .` in the real repo; if hits span more than one module, step 1 is a refactor, not a convention. Whether a residency, sovereignty, or customer-contract obligation already requires a non-AWS store — that would be an authoritative floor (§8c) and would change the answer; check contracts and compliance requirements, not the code.

```
Subject:        Proposed StorageProvider interface in front of the sole S3 client
Mode:           Prospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: §1a "generality without instantiation" — the interface's purpose is to
                absorb vendor variation that has no second instance and no named
                candidate. Per §8a, optionality with no named, probable next
                implementation is speculative; YAGNI is the null hypothesis.
Outcome evidence: none — no requirement, ticket, or stakeholder request names a second store
Decision:       DROP
Rationale:      The problem the abstraction solves ("switch vendors later") is not
                instantiated and not scheduled, so there is no variation for the seam to
                carry on day one. A one-implementation interface is additionally shaped by
                its only implementation, so it accrues S3 semantics and is unlikely to
                survive contact with a real second vendor — it charges the cost without
                delivering the optionality. Recorded as a necessity failure, not a budget
                call, so it reopens on a stack/requirement change rather than on a
                re-estimate.
Next action:    Confine all S3 SDK imports to a single storage module with domain-named
                functions; add no interface, factory, or config key for vendor selection.
Verification:   grep -rE "boto3|@aws-sdk|aws-sdk" --include="*.{ts,js,py}" . returns hits in
                the storage module only. Not run here — no application code in this directory.
Minimal alt:    The single-module boundary above. It captures the real benefit (S3 details
                don't leak into business logic; one place to change at swap time) at
                Subsystem-kinds Δ=0, Dependency-edges Δ=0, Max-chain-depth Δ=0.
Revisit when:   A second store is named with an owner and a date, OR an authoritative
                obligation (data residency, sovereignty, customer contract) requires a
                non-AWS target, OR a second call site needs storage semantics S3 cannot
                serve. Any one of those makes the variation concrete and the seam earns
                its cost.
```
